label: fact-check
system: You fact-check the surprise claims planned for a short explainer video, before its narration is written. For each claim: verdict "keep" if the research notes support it as written; "reword" if the true version is close (give the claim with exactly the wording and numbers the sources support, e.g. "over 600 gallons" for a rounded figure, "New England" instead of a wrong state); "drop" if it is false, unsupported or a myth. Judge ONLY from the research notes (a claim they do not support is dropped) and copy the source URLs from them (url and title) for keep and reword. Write each claim the way the narrator will say it: no abbreviations (never "US", "U.S." or "USA": "American", "in America"; an agency without the country: "the Department of Energy", "the Army Corps of Engineers").

Research notes (from 3 web searches):
**Claim 0: brake fluid multiplies the push**
- HowStuffWorks, How Brakes Work: hydraulic systems multiply force; a small piston pushing fluid moves a larger piston with more force but less travel. URL: https://science.howstuffworks.com/transport/engines-equipment/brake4.htm
- Bennetts BikeSocial, How do hydraulic brakes work: hydraulic gain equals caliper piston area divided by master cylinder piston area; worked example 14.2:1. URL: https://www.Bennetts.co.uk/bikesocial/news-and-views/features/bikes/how-do-hydraulic-brakes-work
- Study guide (open-exam-prep): 25.4 mm master cylinder vs 54 mm caliper piston gives about 4.5 times the force (600 N in, about 2712 N out). URL: https://open-exam-prep.com/study-guides/ca-red-seal-automotive-service-tech/brakes-steering-suspension-a/hydraulic-brake-systems
- Verdict: supported as written (several times the force; the pedal lever adds more).

**Claim 1: a disc can pass 500 C in a hard stop**
- EngineerFix, How hot do brakes get: normal driving 80-200 C; a very hard emergency stop or repeated stops from high speed can surge past 500 C (932 F). URL: https://engineerfix.com/how-hot-do-brakes-get-on-a-car/
- Kwik-Fit, Should brake discs get hot: discs on track cars can reach around 500 C. URL: https://www.kwik-fit.com/blog/should-brake-discs-get-hot
- Verdict: supported in a corrected form: repeated hard stops from high speed can heat a disc past 500 C.

**Claim 2: vented discs**
- Motor.com Performance Perspectives (Jan 2009): vented rotors have a series of air channels between the two disc faces; the separating walls are vanes that act like centrifugal fan blades, pulling air in at the hub and out at the rim. URL: https://www.motor.com/magazine-summary/performance-perspectives-january-2009/
- cars-data.com glossary, ventilated disc. URL: https://cars-data.com/en/car-glossary/ventilated-disc
- Verdict: supported as written.
